nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 5 — Drive It From a Browser
nodes.rationale: Ten gates, not eight. Every task names a code change that makes its new test fail, runs it, captures the real output, and reverts byte-identically with md5sum before and after: a test whose mutation was never run is not a test. The plan is amended in place where execution proved a brief wrong, with the stale text called out rather than silently replaced.

nodes.label: SourceReader
nodes.rationale: A read-only handle with no WorkerRole, no put and no remove. It is not SourceStore because reading stored bytes for a user who asked for those exact bytes is not the open path, and the write surface is the half WorkerRole is worth spending on. Its decode flag is zstd_level != 0, corrected from > 0 — zstd spells --fast=N levels negative and a negative level still produces a frame, so > 0 would hand a compressed frame to a user as their file.

nodes.label: GET /api/revisions/{id}/download
nodes.rationale: variant=original returns byte-identical ingested bytes, making 'downloads are never silently converted' testable for the first time. Order of operations matters: resolve, 404, validate variant, 500 on an unrecorded zstd_level naming the blob, read, re-hash and 500 on mismatch, touch_blob, respond. The two 500 branches stay separate because their messages are — one says an operator has a blob row no ingest path wrote, the other says the bytes on disk are not the bytes we recorded.

nodes.label: check_open_path_boundary
nodes.rationale: Greps for literal type names in lapidary-api: SourceStore is forbidden outright, and SourceReader may appear only in a file whose path ends download.rs. A boundary expressed as a per-file allowance rather than a blanket ban, so the one route that legitimately reads source bytes is named and every other one still fails the gate.

nodes.label: RFC 5987 Content-Disposition
nodes.rationale: Both an ASCII fallback and filename*=UTF-8'' encoding, with the filename synthesized and sanitized for path separators, control characters and quotes. The fixture uses a real Turkish part name rather than an ASCII one with a comment about Turkish. The encoder's allowlist is load-bearing: adding %, ' and * left the suite green while reintroducing a path traversal through RFC 8187 client decoding.

nodes.label: JobPayload::ScanDirectory
nodes.rationale: A deliberate reversal of scan.rs's own module doc, recorded where that reasoning is written and not only in the plan. The original brief could not have been built: enqueue_scan takes a path list produced by walking /ingest, which the api container does not mount. What makes the reversal honest rather than convenient is that the module doc's objection — a failure goes unseen — is answered by rendering the failure reasons, which batch_status already returned and nothing displayed. Alternatives rejected: a Caddy route to worker:8081 spans the browser's API surface across two backends with no gate watching the pattern; mounting /ingest on the api puts the ingest directory on the container whose whole point is reading metadata and derivatives.

nodes.label: enqueue_into
nodes.rationale: enqueue mints a fresh BatchId every call, so a scan job enqueuing its files into a new batch would let the UI poll the scan's own batch, see 1 of 1 complete, and report a finished scan while 150 files are still ingesting. The scan job puts its children in its own batch instead, which works because batch_status computes the aggregate rather than caching a stored total.

nodes.label: Storage Visibility
nodes.rationale: PartSummary grows revision, source_hash, source_bytes, stored_bytes and compressed via one more LATERAL — no migration, every column already on blob. The verifying SELECT is deliberately not the obvious one: sum over the distinct blobs a library's file rows reference, because summing the file rows double-counts a deduplicated library, and add sum(octet_length(thumb_bytes)) because every thumbnail is inline and has no blob row.
